findings.title: Rendering a small DOCX table can exhaust host memory
findings.summary:
An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates the existing one-billion-column, 4,000,000,000-byte f32-vector framing through both span and row-skip inputs; these are static counts.
 Assigned discovery-0032 corroborates the live span and both synthetic row-skip paths, including merge-slot expansion; separate Markdown span clamping does not protect rendering.
findings.remediation:
Enforce practical per-span and total-column budgets for gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before excessive RawCell, column, preference or merge allocation/work. Use checked occupancy sums and col+span arithmetic, apply the same budget to every derived table vector, and return a typed resource-limit refusal on excess. Propagate a caller-adjustable semantic column limit through all public rendering surfaces and charge later column/merge vectors to that same budget.
Additional retained remediation detail: Enforce explicit maximum live cell spans, row skips, aggregate table columns and merge slots before any allocation. Use checked sums and a cumulative layout resource budget, returning a typed refusal when exceeded.

findings.title: Processing renamed auxiliary XML bypasses XML depth limits
findings.summary: A DOCX author can put deeply nested auxiliary XML under a non-.xml/.rels suffix. Admission drains those bytes without XML policy, while rendering, revision listing, revision acceptance/rejection and comparison follow internal relationships and recursively build a DOM. Confirmed rendering parts include theme, styles, numbering, comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; get_revisions and comparison also parse renamed footnotes/endnotes. A small admitted package can terminate the native host or trap WASM. The assigned source additionally confirms eager relationship-selected fontTable parsing before font inspection, including renamed fontTable.bin. Comparison preprocessing also follows renamed styles and charts, alongside footnotes/endnotes. The assigned Standard source additionally identifies edit initialization's existing_comment_ids on relationship-selected comments before the later checked CommentFamily loader. Assigned discovery-0019 corroborates the same shared selector for styles, theme, numbering and fontTable under .bin names; its proof is limited to those four consumers, while earlier validated consumer paths remain retained. Assigned discovery-0027 additionally confirms relationship-selected settings bytes reaching settings_dom/settings_dom_xml and unchecked DOM construction on cache miss; settings is now a supplied validated consumer, whereas earlier recommendations remain historical source limitations. Assigned discovery-0028 supplies already-validated linked-textbox and diagram consumers: relationship-ID media targets at src/convert/mod.rs:17417-17428 and :17453-17464 are decoded and recursively parsed regardless of filename. The new source corroborates fontTable, theme, styles, numbering, settings, comments, notes and header/footer paths, and records that admission's content-type check covers the main part only. Assigned discovery-0031 additionally preserves strict normalization's extension-based pass-through: a relationship-selected fonts.bin remains unmodified before eager fontTable parsing. The raw unchecked parser's documented caller obligations are not themselves the finding.
findings.remediation: Apply active InputLimits at a centralized checked XML access/parse boundary for every semantic XML consumer regardless of filename, or resolve/classify and admit XML through actual content-type/relationship use. Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; explicitly cover the now supplied validated settings_dom/settings_dom_xml cache-miss consumer, with earlier settings-only recommendations retained as historical source limitations. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported. Include linked-textbox and diagram relationship targets in the mandatory filename-independent checked XML boundary before parse_xdocument and in regression coverage. These are now supplied validated affected consumers from discovery-0028; earlier sources' proposed-only status remains historical. Cover revision_processor RevisionIds collection and process_part for all six selected auxiliary buckets (headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles), including public revision acceptance/rejection. Explicitly include the now-confirmed fontTable loader (src/convert/font_table.rs:66-78; src/convert/mod.rs:806) in the mandatory checked XML boundary; parsing must be bounded before any font root/entry inspection. Explicitly cover comparison defined_style_ids (src/document_comparer.rs:4684-4696), relationship-selected footnotes/endnotes (4724-4750) and chart preprocessing (4861-4878), all reached through admitted nonidentical comparison inputs (6555-6569,6607-6625). Apply the same mandatory XML boundary before edit initialization's existing_comment_ids scan, not only in the later checked CommentFamily loader; preserve the effective checks at inspect::parse_part_within and edit::load_stories. Enforce the same checked boundary before settings DOM cache population, and preserve valid bounded nonstandard auxiliary filenames.

findings.title: Large Chicago numbering values can exhaust memory while reading or rendering a DOCX
findings.summary:
An untrusted DOCX can select Chicago numbering with a huge list start/startOverride or section page start. The shared chicago_label formatter repeats a UTF-8 symbol roughly n/4 times without a length bound, allowing gigabyte allocations during list rendering, ordinary section-page processing and Markdown numbered-list views. Authored endnote starts also reach this shared formatter. The supplied u32::MAX framing selects 1073741824 double-daggers, about 3 GiB of UTF-8 label bytes; this is static arithmetic. Additional supplied static framing: start=2147483647 selects 536870912 UTF-8 double-daggers (‡), requesting 1.5 GiB of marker bytes before downstream copies.
 Assigned discovery-0032 additionally supplies start=4294967294: 1073741824 daggers (†), about 3 GiB of UTF-8 before copies. Level-zero reader/agent labels reach the shared formatter without a large ilvl.
findings.remediation:
Bound generated byte/glyph length inside the shared Chicago formatter before repetition, with a documented safe cycle/fallback or typed refusal. Apply that bound to all list, startOverride, section-page and Markdown/direct list_number callers; do not rely on input bytes, counter saturation or later clipping. Include authored endnote numStart/format and MCP agent-view callers in the shared formatter budget.
Additional retained remediation detail: Apply a central maximum output length to Chicago labels before repetition and enforce a cumulative numbering-output budget. Use a documented bounded fallback or typed refusal consistently for list, read/agent, page and future formatter consumers.

findings.title: Aliased legacy DOC pieces expand small physical text into enormous logical stories
findings.summary:
Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements. Supplied discovery-0023 additionally gives 4096 contiguous one-million-character pieces sharing a 1 MB physical range (4096000000 logical characters within u32). Public read/conversion and native read_document refusal-hint parsing reach the same expansion before returning a format diagnostic; no runtime resource measurement is claimed. Additional supplied static framing: 4096 pieces reusing one 64 KiB compressed extent describe 268435456 logical characters; continuity and source-bound checks permit the reuse. This is not a measured allocation. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies 4000 one-million-character logical pieces sharing about 1 MB of physical text with about 48 KB of piece metadata, requesting about four billion StoryChars. CP continuity, checked offsets and physically bounded CFB traversal do not bound logical expansion; counts are static.
 Assigned discovery-0032 supplies 65535 contiguous pieces of 65535 compressed characters sharing one 65535-byte physical range: 4294836225 logical CPs within u32 and about 786 KB of piece records. These are static counts.
findings.remediation:
Introduce configurable legacy physical-input, piece-count, cumulative logical-character, retained-metadata and expansion-work budgets. Check FIB ccp_text and checked cumulative piece lengths before materialization, charge every decoded character including repeated physical aliases, and return typed refusals through read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and CLI callers. Preserve legitimate fast-save aliases and split UTF-16 surrogate handling within budget. Replace full legacy parsing used only for diagnostic refusal hints with a cheap bounded probe, or apply the same logical/work budgets before that parser runs.
Additional retained remediation detail: Introduce a configurable legacy logical-character/output budget, check ccp_text and cumulative decoded piece work before materialization, and enforce it during decoding. Preserve valid reuse while returning a typed refusal for excessive expansion.

findings.title: Cyclic Markdown drawing dependencies terminate conversion through unbounded recursion
findings.summary: A drawing: image destination in ordinary Markdown is base64-decoded and deserialized into a dependency graph without validation. Package materialization recursively follows each dep.rels.part before writing the dependent part and has no active-node or completed-node map. A one-node self-reference causes indefinite recursion and stack exhaustion, even with default Markdown conversion options and no image loader. Header/footer drawing payloads also reach this same materializer through view_stories::story_part. Capture memoizes a part before descending, so even capture-produced envelopes can encode a cycle; capture count/byte limits do not establish an acyclic imported graph. The supplied discovery-0030 trace additionally records that an empty boxes collection bypasses text-box-specific Writer finish checks; these checks do not validate the dependency graph.
findings.remediation: Validate dependency indices, count/byte/depth limits and graph shape at import. Materialize with an active/completed traversal state and index-to-output map, rejecting cycles or reserving identities to support cycles without recursive expansion. Memoize shared subgraphs. Enforce explicit dependency-edge and traversal-work budgets before assembly; when rejecting active-node revisits return a typed conversion refusal. Apply the same graph validation and traversal state to header/footer drawing materialization, not only body drawings.

findings.title: Repeated relationship IDs trigger quadratic repair work
findings.summary: Opening a package repairs identical duplicate relationship IDs. For n distinct IDs each repeated identically, each repair linearly searches an increasingly long Vec, producing quadratic CPU work on shallow metadata that fits existing byte and attribute limits. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies approximately 200000 shallow Relationship records with 100000 distinct identical duplicate pairs within a 64 MiB part, implying about five billion membership comparisons. Conflicting duplicates remain promptly refused; counts are static.
findings.remediation: Track already-reported duplicate IDs in a HashSet or alongside seen-map state, retaining a Vec only for deterministic reporting order. Optionally cap relationship-record/work totals before repair; test many distinct identical duplicate pairs while preserving deterministic repaired-ID order and conflicting-duplicate refusals. Apply an active relationship-record/work budget at metadata admission in addition to making duplicate membership near-linear.

findings.title: Python and Node plan recording can overwrite unrelated files through staging symlinks
findings.summary:
The Python and Node CLIs write plans through a predictable .<plan>.<PID>.partial pathname using nonexclusive truncating writes. A local actor who can create entries in the plan directory can preplace a symlink there and make the victim overwrite another file it can write, before the intended plan replacement.
 Assigned discovery-0032 corroborates both non-dry-run recorders after successful plan preview. Intentional final-plan symlink resolution is distinct from the independently substituted staging entry.
findings.remediation:
Use exclusive, unpredictable staging owned by a private directory, hold the opened handle through writing, and rename that verified file. Reuse the native publication design or equivalent mkstemp/exclusive wx APIs and never follow existing staging entries. Python can reuse native publication; Node needs equivalent secure publication semantics. Preserve intentional final-plan symlink resolution to its authorized resolved target while securing the separate staging object; successful recording installs a verified regular plan file and failure preserves prior output.
Additional retained remediation detail: Use an exclusively created private staging directory/file held by handle, verify staged bytes, and atomically publish to the authorized plan target. Refuse preexisting staging objects and preserve intended final-plan symlink semantics without following a staging symlink.

findings.title: Tolerated XML syntax can hide recursive elements from admission
findings.summary: A DOCX author can place nested element text inside an XML comment after an unquoted attribute. Admission counts only shallow quick-xml events, while the permissive DOM parser consumes that attribute differently and recursively interprets the hidden tags. The normal .xml path can therefore exhaust the host stack despite max_xml_depth.
findings.remediation: Make admission and DOM construction consume the same grammar, reject unsupported DTDs at package admission, parse unquoted values correctly or refuse them, and enforce a hard depth budget inside DOM construction.
